annotation.title_clean: Notice to the Parties and the Profession: The Use of Artificial Intelligence in Court Proceedings
annotation.title_en: Notice to the Parties and the Profession: The Use of Artificial Intelligence in Court Proceedings
annotation.summary_en: Federal Court of Canada notice (7 May 2024) requiring parties to declare in the first paragraph when filed litigation documents contain AI-generated content. It sets principles of caution, human verification and neutrality, and commits the Court not to use automated decision-making without public consultation.
key_provisions_or_claims: Mandatory Declaration in first paragraph where content is generated directly by generative AI
No declaration needed where AI only suggests changes to human-authored content
Principles: caution with AI legal references, human in the loop verification, neutrality (no adverse inference)
Signing party remains responsible for accuracy of filed material
Court will not use AI for decisions without public consultation; AI Working Group consults stakeholders
